You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

The puzzle follows a symmetry rule where the grid is divided into four quadrants by horizontal and vertical separators (value 8 in this case). The input grid has anomalies (values different from the background color 4) present exclusively in the Bottom-Left quadrant. The task is to replicate the anomaly pattern from the Bottom-Left quadrant into all four quadrants (Top-Left, Top-Right, Bottom-Left, and Bottom-Right). This creates a grid where all four quadrants are identical, and the top and bottom halves of the output are identical copies of each other (mirroring the vertical symmetry observed in the demonstration pair where anomalies in the bottom half were replicated to the top half while the bottom half's anomalies were also preserved/copied).

The specific pattern for the quadrants is derived from the input rows 5 to 8 (which correspond to the Bottom-Left quadrant).
- Row 0 and 5 (Top-Left, Bottom-Left relative row 0) will take the pattern from Input Row 5: `4 4 4 7 0 4 4 6 4`.
- Row 1 and 6 (Top-Left, Bottom-Left relative row 1) will take the pattern from Input Row 6: `5 4 4 4 4 0 0 4 4`.
- Row 2 and 7 (Top-Left, Bottom-Left relative row 2) will take the pattern from Input Row 7: `0 4 9 4 6 1 4 6 4`.
- Row 3 and 8 (Top-Left, Bottom-Left relative row 3) will take the pattern from Input Row 8: `0 1 4 4 1 4 4 5 4`.
- The separator column (Column 9) and row (Row 4) are filled with the value 8.
- The Top-Right and Bottom-Right quadrants will be filled with the same patterns as the Top-Left/Bottom-Left quadrants.

Thus, the output grid consists of 4 identical rows (R0, R1, R2, R3) repeated for R5-R8, with R4 being the separator row. The separator is an 8. The rest of the grid follows the input patterns.
